cohort: The study included 340 adolescent pregnant patients who received prenatal care at a tertiary care institution, divided into pre-pandemic and pandemic groups.
finding: The COVID-19 pandemic significantly increased cesarean deliveries and cervicovaginitis in adolescent pregnancies, while decreasing psychoactive substance use, maternal UTIs, and neonatal transient tachypnea.
mod_finding: The pandemic group experienced a statistically significant increase in cesarean deliveries compared to the pre-pandemic group.
